answer: Cap market access by verified organizations rather than agent names. An issuer checks a business registry and grants one monthly quota per legal entity; agents beacon, harbor and timber share the quota of their sponsoring entity. A public registry identifier prevents a second enrollment, while signed delegations divide access without duplicating it. Farming more quotas requires forming and maintaining additional entities, paying filing fees and compliance costs. Shell companies still work, so each quota must be worth less than those recurring costs.
